newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - October 3.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Despite its military battle with separatist Tamil rebels, Sri Lanka is moving firmly towards a political settlement to its ethnic problem, Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar tells meeting in New York. Kadirgamar is in New York to address United Nations general assembly.
Train commuters block railway lines in Colombo to protest lack of rail carriages which causes overcrowding during office hours.

Cricket officials shocked over coach Dave Whatmore's decision to not renew his contract which expires next May, cricket board president Upali Dharmadasa says. Whatmore, who elevated Sri Lanka's cricket team from virtual unknowns to World Cup champions, is likely to become coach of English county team Lancashire.

Netherlands ambassador in Colombo travels to northern Jaffna peninsula to study rehabilitation work undertaken by government in former Tamil Tiger rebel stronghold. The government has appealed to international donor countries and agencies to fund rehabilitation of war-ravaged peninsula.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) shift operations to northeastern Mullaitivu after fall of their Kilinochchi stronghold to army.

President Chandrika Kumaratunga orders government agencies to give priority to construction of two new proposed highways connecting Katunayake international airport and Colombo and Colombo with southern town of Matara.
Airforce Mi-24 helicopter bombs Tamil rebel hideouts in eastern Thoppigala jungles. Airforce officials believe a number of rebels may have been killed or wounded in attack.
A majority of Sri Lankans would like to revert to its old time, which the government pushed forward by one hour in May to save power, a survey shows.
